cues.text: Hi Howard ... I haven’t seen you for a while.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Hi Joanne. Yeah, they’re keeping us really busy on the postgraduate programme. But how are you? You’ll be starting your dissertation soon, won’t you?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yeah ... tutorials start next week ... I’ve got Dr Peterson. You’ll remember it all from last year, of course!
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: It’s not something you forget easily. But seriously, although I didn’t expect to enjoy writing my dissertation ... and in fact I didn’t really find it much fun, I wouldn’t have missed the experience ...I found it really improved my understanding of the whole degree programme, you know, from the first year on ...
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: So what are you doing yours on?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Glaciated landscapes ... although I haven’t decided exactly what aspect yet.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: I did mine on climate systems, so I can’t help you much I’m afraid. But you’ll be fine once you start your tutorials ... Dr Peterson’ll help you focus.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: I know, and he’ll set me deadlines for the different stages ... which is what I need. My concern is that I’ve got tons of material on the topic, and I won’t be able to stick to the word limit, you know.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Hmm. I remember I had different concerns when I was doing my dissertation.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Last year?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yeah ... before my first tutorial I did a lot of fairly general reading ‘cause I hadn’t fixed on my topic at that stage. I actually enjoyed that quite a lot and really improved my reading speed, you know, so I was getting through a lot of material. I was frightened I wouldn’t remember it all though so I got into the habit of making very detailed notes.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: So did you find your tutor helpful .in getting you started?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yeah we certainly had some interesting discussions but it’s funny ... I saw a brilliant programme about climate change and it was that that really fired me up. It was talking about some recent research which seemed to contradict some of the articles I’d been reading.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Hmmm.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: So you say your tutorials start next week?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yeah.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well, the first month’s crucial. You’ve got to meet your tutor and decide on your focus but don’t become too dependent on him...you know, don’t see him every week...only when you want to check something.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Once you’ve got the focus you’ve got to get reading - it’s helpful to look through the bibliographies for all the course modules relating to your topic. And get hold of any books you think you’ll need.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: I haven’t got much money ...
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: I mean get the books from the library, far better.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: And I suppose I should prepare a detailed outline of the chapters?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Yeah absolutely . but don’t feel you have to follow it slavishly . it’s meant to be flexible.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Okay. Now, I’m someone who likes to get writing quickly ... I can’t just sit and read for a month.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Not like me then ... but if that’s what suits you, you know, your natural approach, then you really ought to start immediately and write the first chapter ...
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Right.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Now Joanne, about the library ... it’s worthwhile getting on good terms with the staff ... they aren’t always helpful with undergraduates .
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: I suppose they focus on post-grads more.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Maybe . but show them you’re serious about wanting to do good work.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: And what if I can’t find what I need?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well, there’s inter-library loans ...
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Borrowing books from other libraries ... but I’ve heard it isn’t all that reliable.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: You’re right.. .but you probably won’t need it anyway ... be positive, the library is likely to have most things you need ... and during the dissertation writing period, you can take out fifteen instead of the usual ten books.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Should I look at previous years’ dissertations?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: You can do .
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: But I won’t know which are the good ones.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: The library only keeps the best and the staff can advise you.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Are they willing to do that?
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Oh yeah .
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: And I’m worried about getting journal articles ... from the electronic library.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well, have you tried to find any yet?
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: No.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well you should . it’s really straightforward.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: That’s obviously something I’ll have to look into.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Dr Peterson will help.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Yeah, I know I can go to him if I have any worries.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Except he will be away in the second month - it’s the holidays. You should ask him what to do while he’s away.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Gosh, yeah ... but I suppose I can get a lot of support from coursemates ... I know a couple of people who are thinking of doing the same topic as me.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Take care, collaboration can become dependency. I think you’d better see how that works out what the people are like.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: You’re probably right ... About other reading, I suppose Dr Peterson’ll recommend plenty of good articles to get me started.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: One thing I’d find out is what his attitude is to internet sources.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: Surely not in this day and age? I’d better get that sorted out right at the beginning.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: I would if I were you.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: And I’ve also got some questions about the research sections - how much time I should spend explaining the process.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: Well, I think that’s up to you ... you can see how it develops as you’re writing.
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: OK.
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: It’s the same with things like time management . that’s something a tutor can’t really help you with .
cues.speaker: Man

cues.text: I agree!
cues.speaker: Woman

cues.text: So is there anything else you need me to go over .
cues.speaker: Man
